turns.doctor_question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Well, I came in because I keep getting these nagging thoughts. I'm a designer, and I just keep worrying that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or maybe that I sent the wrong version of a file to a client. And... even when I check and can see that it’s probably fine, my mind just keeps circling back to it. It's just getting a bit frustrating to deal with.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient reports recurrent, persistent, and intrusive nagging thoughts and doubts about making mistakes or sending the wrong files, which their mind repeatedly circles back to despite checking.

turns.doctor_question: When these thoughts about mistakes pop up, do they feel intrusive and unwanted?
turns.patient_response: Yes, they definitely do. Like I was just saying, they really are just these nagging thoughts that force their way in. I don't want to be thinking about a tiny layout mistake or worrying if I sent the wrong file, especially after I've already checked and know it's fine. But... yeah, they just keep popping up anyway, and my mind just loops back to them no matter how much I try to push them away.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient confirms having persistent, intrusive, and unwanted thoughts about making mistakes that keep popping up despite attempts to push them away.

turns.doctor_question: When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself repeatedly checking your work or sent files to relieve the anxiety?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Before I submit any work now, I’ll usually re-open the file, compare all the layers, and re-save it. And sometimes I'll just... mentally walk through every single design choice one more time to make sure it's right. It’s not like it takes over my whole day or anything, but it definitely makes me slower. It just makes me feel a bit less free creatively when I have to do all that just to settle my nerves.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly confirms performing repetitive checking behaviors (re-opening files, comparing layers, re-saving) and mental acts (reviewing design choices) to reduce anxiety and settle their nerves.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel that the amount of checking you do is excessive?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I suppose I do. I mean, like I was just saying about having to re-open the files and compare all the layers... it's probably more than most people do. Even though it doesn't take over my entire day, having to mentally walk through every single design choice again just to hit 'send' is... well, it's a bit much. It just slows me down and makes the whole process feel less creative and more like a chore. So, yeah, it does feel a bit excessive to me.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive checking behaviors and mental review rituals that they recognize as excessive and slowing them down.

turns.doctor_question: About how much time do these thoughts and checking rituals take up in a typical day?
turns.patient_response: I'd say... maybe about an hour total throughout the day. It's not like I sit down for a solid hour just checking things. It's more like ten minutes here before I send an email, fifteen minutes there double-checking a layout. It adds up, but it's spread out, so it doesn't completely derail my whole schedule. Just enough to be annoying.

turns.doctor_question: If you try not to do the extra checking, do you become very anxious that something bad has been missed?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, definitely. If I try to just hit send without doing all that... the anxiety spikes pretty quickly. Like I mentioned before, I really feel like I have to re-open the file, check all the layers, and mentally review every single design choice. If I try to skip that process, I just get this overwhelming feeling that I've missed a glaring mistake that's going to ruin the project. I know I said it doesn't take up my whole day, but the anxiety of *not* doing it is strong enough that it's just easier to do the checking, even though it makes me slower and stifles my creativity.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient confirms engaging in repetitive checking behaviors and mental reviews (re-opening files, checking layers, reviewing design choices) driven by overwhelming anxiety that a mistake has been made.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel these repeated checking thoughts and urges are unreasonable or excessive, even while you’re having them?
turns.patient_response:
I'm not really sure about that. I mean, we just talked about how it's probably more than most people do, so I know it's excessive in general. But... right when I'm actually having the urge to check the design files? It doesn't really feel unreasonable to me in that exact moment. 

When I'm in the middle of it, it just feels completely necessary. It's usually only after the fact, or when I realize it's slowing my work down again, that I step back and think it's a bit much. But while the thoughts are actually happening, no, I just feel like I absolutely have to do it.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of your design work, do you also find yourself worrying a lot about other parts of life?
turns.patient_response: Um, no, not really. It seems to just be tied to my design work. I don't really find myself worrying excessively about other things... like, you know, everyday stuff, bills, or my health. It's pretty much just when I'm at my computer working on a project that I get stuck doing all that checking. Outside of work, things feel pretty normal.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies excessive or generalized worry about everyday matters, bills, or health outside of work.

turns.doctor_question: If you could be completely certain your design was correct without doing the extra checking, would you still feel a need to check it again?
turns.patient_response:
No, I don't think I would. If I could somehow just... know for a fact that there weren't any mistakes, I'd be happy to just send it off. 

The only reason I do all that extra checking is because I'm trying to get to that feeling of being certain. I'm looking for the mistakes I'm worried I made. So, yeah, if I already knew it was 100 percent correct, I wouldn't feel any need to go back through the files again.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes persistent doubt and worry about having made mistakes in their work that drives a need for certainty.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive 'extra checking' behaviors in an attempt to alleviate doubt and achieve a feeling of certainty.
